ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows propene, CH3CH=CH2, reacting with Br2 and H2O to form CH3CH(OH)CH2Br. In the product, the OH group is attached to the internal carbon originally in the double bond, and the Br atom is attached to the terminal CH2 carbon. Reasoning: The internal alkene carbon next to CH3 is the more substituted alkene carbon, while the terminal CH2 carbon is the less substituted alkene carbon. For bromohydrin/HOBr addition, the Markovnikov regioselectivity convention is that OH goes to the more substituted carbon and Br goes to the less substituted carbon. The product shown matches that arrangement, so the orientation is Markovnikov.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Br2/H2O or NBS in aqueous solvent forms a bromonium-ion/bromohydrin pathway. In an unsymmetrical bromonium ion, the more substituted carbon bears greater positive character, so water attacks that carbon; after deprotonation, OH is installed at the more substituted carbon. This corresponds to Markovnikov regioselectivity for bromohydrin formation, even though Br is on the less substituted carbon.
